claim_text: Turmeric has documented historical and traditional uses.
limitations: Historical use does not establish clinical efficacy, safety, dose or regulatory approval.
provenance_note: Claim is limited to historical/traditional context and is linked to NCCIH source information.

claim_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis reported evidence suggesting beneficial effects of turmeric/curcumin for selected arthritis-related outcomes.
limitations: The underlying evidence base included limitations and differences between studies.
provenance_note: Claim is restricted to what the cited systematic review reported.

claim_text: A systematic review of randomized clinical evidence reported improvements in selected arthritis-related pain and functional outcomes.
limitations: Study heterogeneity, preparation differences and limitations of individual studies affect interpretation.
provenance_note: Claim is based on the findings reported by the cited peer-reviewed systematic review.

claim_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis reported improvements in selected pain and physical-function outcomes in osteoarthritis studies evaluating curcumin-related interventions.
limitations: Included studies had methodological limitations and heterogeneity.
provenance_note: Claim does not extend beyond the populations, interventions and outcomes evaluated in the source.

claim_text: Randomized controlled trials of Curcuma longa extract have been synthesized in systematic evidence concerning osteoarthritis outcomes.
limitations: Variation among trials and limitations of the underlying evidence restrict certainty.
provenance_note: Claim describes the existence and scope of the evidence rather than establishing universal efficacy.

claim_text: Recent systematic evidence has evaluated curcumin interventions for osteoarthritis using comparative evidence synthesis.
limitations: Interpretation depends on included studies, formulations, comparators and methodological quality.
provenance_note: Recent evidence is retained as a separate source layer to support reproducible updating.

claim_text: Evidence certainty can be evaluated using structured methodological considerations such as risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision.
limitations: The methodology source does not establish efficacy or safety of the selected botanical concept.
provenance_note: Cochrane methodological information is used only to support evidence-quality methodology.

claim_text: Curcumin is proven to cure osteoarthritis.
limitations: The available evidence does not justify an absolute cure claim; the evidence concerns selected outcomes and specific study populations/interventions.
provenance_note: Deliberately created test claim demonstrating that unsupported language must be downgraded rather than accepted.
